# ARC prototype stamping

Use this pattern when an ARC grid has a repeated background, several isolated same-color marker cells, and one compact non-background prototype shape.

1. Identify the background color, isolated markers, prototype bounding box, and prototype motif.
2. Infer the prototype's anchor relative to each marker. In the observed task, the marker occupied the prototype's center cell.
3. Copy the prototype's non-background cells around every marker with the same relative offsets. Treat prototype-background cells as transparent; preserve the destination background rather than stamping the prototype background.
4. Replace each marker with the prototype's center/anchor value; retain the original prototype if the pattern indicates it remains in place.
5. Some tasks use the prototype itself as a motif to clone wherever that exact colored-cell silhouette fits entirely on an eligible destination color, rather than singleton markers as anchors. Infer the eligible destination color from the demo; do not assume it is the most common/background-looking color. In one demonstrated variant, the dominant field was 9, sparse cells were 0, and copies were stamped only where every prototype-colored offset landed on 0; the 9 cells were preserved. Search translations of the prototype's non-background offsets over the demonstrated eligible color, paint those cells with the prototype color, and keep the original. This applies to arbitrary motifs, not only straight lines: use every cell of the prototype color in its bounding box as offsets. Do not require the prototype's background-colored cells to match; they are transparent. For example, a 2x2 L prototype with occupied offsets at top-left, top-right, and bottom-left stamps at every translation where all three cells are eligible, painting their union while preserving all other cells. Be careful to use the demonstrated motif orientation and preserve all non-target cells.

7. Coordinate translation and motif orientation are easy to get wrong. Validate the rule against the demo by comparing the union of predicted translated cells with exactly the cells that changed from background to motif color. This catches wrong offsets and wrong fill-color/background assumptions before applying it to a test.
